title: Units before speed: what a dataflow-versus-von-Neumann benchmark actually measures, and what to report instead
description: A measurement-methodology note on the benchmark published by kostyk348/tensor-broth, which compares a von Neumann interpreter loop with a 3D spatial dataflow engine and reads the resulting table as a paradigm verdict. The two columns count different things: VM instructions (one cell write each) against 27-tap multiply-accumulates over three channels (81 per voxel update). Converted to a common unit the implied 1138-fold advantage becomes 5.3-fold at the reported cube size and 14.4-fold at twice the edge length. A second axis separates paradigm from implementation: at one fixed cube the dependency-free NumPy backend of the same engine is 3.5 times faster than the torch path the code calls the fast one. The deposit contains the experiment plan, the harness (Rust, standard library only), the raw logs of every run, the derived quantities, the number ledger and the LaTeX source.
notes: Every number in the note is generated by the accompanying harness from raw logs; every reference was resolved by a machine query before it was cited. See verify_all.sh.
